info.title: QbAutopost API
info.description:
Turns a job folder or a batch of JSON rows into posted QuickBooks Desktop transactions.

This document is **hand-authored** (`src/QbAutopost.Api/wwwroot/openapi.json`): .NET 8 has no built-in OpenAPI generator and Swashbuckle is excluded, so nothing generates it from the code. It is kept honest by `OpenApiDriftTests`, which walks the application's own route table and fails the build when a route is undocumented, an operation has no route, or an operation is missing its summary, its response schema or the scope it needs. `x-required-scope` on each operation is the scope the middleware actually enforces, not a description of it.

The reference page and this document are served only when `Api:Reference:Enabled` is true, and both need the `health:read` scope.

get.summary: Liveness and build facts; never calls QuickBooks or Hermes.
get.description: Answers from in-process state only, so a monitor may poll it every few seconds and still get an answer while a post holds the QuickBooks gateway.

get.summary: Readiness: settings, prompts, rules, lists, log folder and the job worker.
get.description: `ok` is false only when a check of severity `error` failed; a `warning` keeps `ok` true.

503.description: At least one error-severity check failed.

get.summary: QuickBooks SDK registration, versions and bitness; no company file is opened.
get.description: Answers while QuickBooks is closed, while another company is open, or while a certificate dialog is pending — this is the check that explains a failure that never reached QuickBooks.

200.description: The request processor is registered and the bitness matches.

503.description: The SDK is not usable; `message` says why.

get.summary: One round trip to QuickBooks: is the expected company file open?
get.description: Opens an SDK session, so it waits behind a post in progress for at most `QuickBooks:BusyTimeoutSeconds`.

get.summary: Hermes reachability, model name and round-trip latency.
get.description: With `Hermes:Enabled` false the app runs with no model at all and this reports the disabled client.

post.summary: A full session round trip, timed step by step.
post.description: Its own budget (`QuickBooks:ConnectionTestTimeoutSeconds`, default 180 s), deliberately longer than the busy timeout: on the owner's server a certificate dialog held the first session 101 s, and a slow answer is not a broken one. Changes nothing.

200.description: The round trip finished; `ok` and `steps` say how it went.

post.summary: Is this company file the configured one, open in QuickBooks, and backed up?
post.description: Read-only: no qbXML is sent. A *different* company file open in QuickBooks is an error, not a warning — it is the one misconfiguration that posts real money into the wrong ledger.

422.description: A check of severity `error` failed; the body lists every check.

post.summary: Would these rows post? The same reader, mapper and gates, stopping short of the SDK call.
post.description: Offline and never writes, so a batch can be checked while the QuickBooks server is shut down. 400 when the request contradicts itself (a control total that does not add up, no rows, too many); 422 when it was understood and a gate held a row.

parameters.name: includeQbXml
parameters.description: Return the qbXML request body as well. It carries every amount and name in the batch, so it is served only to a key holding `qb:debug`; a caller without it is told so rather than left wondering.

422.description: The request was understood and at least one row was held or skipped.

post.summary: Post JSON rows to QuickBooks and return the batch result.
post.description: The only route that sends transactions to QuickBooks. The batch is on disk before it is queued, so there is always something to poll. `dryRun` (default `DryRunDefault`) ends in `ready` with nothing sent. If the work outlasts `Api:SyncPostTimeoutSeconds` the answer is 202 with a batch to poll and the work carries on; `Prefer: respond-async` asks for that immediately.

200.description: The batch finished (or was a dry run).

get.summary: The cached QuickBooks account, vendor and customer names.
get.description: Read from `qb-lists.json`, so it answers while QuickBooks is shut down and never queues behind a post. A `syncedUtc` of `null` with empty lists means the sync has not run yet; it is not an error.

200.description: The names as the last sync left them.

post.summary: Read the QuickBooks account, vendor and customer lists into qb-lists.json.
post.description: One read-only message set (active records only). It runs on the single job worker, so it cannot overlap a job or a post. This is the v1 spelling; `POST /api/v1/qb/sync-lists` is the same handler under the pre-M9 name and will go when the legacy routes do (Q-53, Q-69).

200.description: The lists were read and written.

post.summary: Deprecated spelling of POST /api/v1/quickbooks/lists/sync; same handler, same body.
post.description: Kept because callers written before M9 use it. Move to `/api/v1/quickbooks/lists/sync`; this path goes when `Api:LegacyRoutes` is turned off (Q-53).

200.description: The lists were read and written.

get.summary: The batch as last recorded — the poll target for a post that outlasted its budget.
get.description: Read from `result.json`, falling back to `status.json` while the batch is still running, so the answer survives a restart of this process.

post.summary: Delete the transactions this batch posted, one message set on the job worker.
post.description: Each ledger entry is marked `undone` as QuickBooks confirms its delete, so a partial undo is recorded as exactly what happened.

200.description: What was deleted, and what would not delete.

get.summary: Every known job, newest first, optionally filtered by status.

post.summary: Queue a job folder for analysis (and posting, when it is not a dry run).
post.description: The job id is derived from the folder, so re-submitting the same folder is the same job; `force` re-runs one that already finished.

202.description: The job was accepted and queued.

post.summary: Would this folder run? F1, the statement parse and the G1 reconcile gate, with no job queued.
post.description: Nothing is written into the folder (not even `output/`), no job id is taken and QuickBooks is never called. It stops short of the requirement, the mapper and the duplicate check, so a folder that passes here may still hold lines when it runs.

422.description: The folder would not run; the body is the same shape as the 200.

get.summary: One job: its status, its statements, and what was held, skipped or posted.

post.summary: Post a job that analysed cleanly and is waiting in `ready`.

202.description: The job was queued for posting.

post.summary: Teach the mapper that a description fragment means a named vendor or customer.
post.description: Written atomically into `rules.json` and picked up by the next job or re-post.

200.description: The rule as written, with what it replaced.

post.summary: Teach the mapper which expense account a vendor posts to.
post.description: The account must exist in `qb-lists.json` when the lists have been synced, so a typo is refused here rather than by QuickBooks mid-batch.

200.description: The rule as written, with what it replaced.

get.description: Served only when `Api:Reference:Enabled` is true; otherwise the route is not mapped at all and the answer is 404.

get.summary: The Scalar page that renders this document.
get.description: Served only when `Api:Reference:Enabled` is true. Its script comes from the package, not a CDN, and the "send request" buttons are hidden unless `Api:Reference:AllowTryIt` is true.

apiKeyAuth.name: X-Api-Key
apiKeyAuth.description: `X-Api-Key: <key>` — the header this build reads, and the one every operation is secured with here. Each key belongs to one caller in `clients.json` and carries only the scopes that caller was given; `x-required-scope` on every operation names the one it needs.

bearerAuth.description: `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. api-v1 §2.2 calls this the preferred form and FR-A-18 asks this document to declare it — but **this build does not accept it yet**: `ApiKeyMiddleware` reads only `X-Api-Key`. It is declared, not offered, so no reader is sent down a road the app refuses (Q-67).

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Replaying a request under the same key returns the stored answer and sends nothing to QuickBooks a second time; the same key with a different body is a 409.

BatchId.name: id
BatchId.description: Batch id. It contains `#`, which must be sent percent-encoded as `%23`.

JobId.name: id
JobId.description: Job id, derived from the job folder's name.

BadRequest.description: Malformed or self-inconsistent request. Nothing was posted.

Unauthorized.description: No key, or a key no caller holds.

Forbidden.description: The key is known but lacks the scope this operation needs.

Conflict.description: A state conflict, or an `Idempotency-Key` replayed with a different body.

TooManyRequests.description: Rate limited; `Retry-After` says for how long.

Unavailable.description: QuickBooks or Hermes is unreachable or busy, or the app is not ready.

Problem.description: RFC 7807 problem details. `requestId` is the same id as the `X-Request-Id` header and every log line of that request.

errors.description: Present when the failure is per item.

companyFile.description: Refused unless `QuickBooks:AllowCompanyFileOverride` is on and the path is inside `QuickBooks:AllowedCompanyFolders`.

reference.description: The caller's own name for this batch.

controlTotal.description: The caller's own sum over every submitted row. It is checked, never corrected: a mismatch refuses the whole batch and no amount is adjusted to make it agree.

allowModelAccounts.description: Let the model choose an account for a row no rule resolves. Needs the `qb:post:ai` scope as well.

externalId.description: The caller's key. Echoed and stored; never used to decide identity.

amount.description: Positive, at most two decimals. The direction comes from `kind`.

account.description: The bank or credit-card account the money moves on.

lineAccount.description: The expense or income account; rules resolve it when it is left out.

last4.description: Last four digits of the account; part of the fingerprint.

counts.description: `wouldPost + held + skipped` is `submitted`, so the arithmetic of the answer can be checked too. `duplicates` is part of `skipped`.

unknownNames.description: Names in the batch that `qb-lists.json` does not have.

PlanRow.description: One submitted row and what would become of it.

requestId.description: First 16 characters of the row's fingerprint.

reason.description: The hold or skip code, e.g. `no-account-rule`, `already-in-quickbooks`.

batchId.description: The earlier batch this row already posted in.

posted.description: The money that actually moved; zero for a dry run.

unavailable.description: Nothing was sent: QuickBooks could not be reached, or the backup guard refused. Safe to retry.

location.description: Poll this for the finished batch.

missingInRules.description: Names QuickBooks has that `rules.json` says nothing about.

QbLists.description: The cached QuickBooks names (`qb-lists.json`). Empty lists with a null `syncedUtc` mean the sync has not run.

ok.description: The folder would become a job and no statement was held.

errors.description: Why the folder cannot become a job (F1). Empty when it can.

unreadable.description: Files that will not be read, and why (F4).

layout.description: The `CsvLayouts` name, or `hermes-t2` for a PDF.

reconcile.description: The G1 verdict: `{ ok, verified, message }`.

totals.description: The statement's own printed figures (PDF only).

force.description: Re-run a folder that already finished.

fragment.description: A fragment of the statement description, matched case-insensitively.

name.description: The QuickBooks vendor or customer name.

account.description: A QuickBooks account name; checked against `qb-lists.json` when it exists.

previous.description: What the rule said before; null when it is new.
